successCriteria.description: The notification module exists at src/modules/notification/ with notification.model.ts, notification.repository.ts, notification.service.ts, and an index.ts barrel that re-exports the entity, both interfaces, and both concrete classes.

notification.model.ts declares the Notification entity with exactly these fields and types: id (string), recipientId (string), type (string), title (string), message (string), relatedEntityType (string|null), relatedEntityId (string|null), status ('PENDING'|'SENT'|'READ'|'ARCHIVED'), createdAt (Date), readAt (Date|null) — no extra or missing fields.

notification.model.ts declares INotificationRepository and INotificationService interfaces, and PgNotificationRepository implements INotificationRepository while NotificationService implements INotificationService.

PgNotificationRepository performs all persistence via raw parameterized pg SQL through the shared pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts, with every repository method accepting an optional PoolClient as the last parameter and defaulting to the shared pool when omitted.

The repository maps snake_case DB columns (recipient_id, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, created_at, read_at) to the camelCase entity fields and coerces null/absent relatedEntityType, relatedEntityId, and readAt to null.

NotificationService generates ids via randomUUID() and sets createdAt at write time, coercing absent relatedEntityType/relatedEntityId/readAt to null, and passes the optional client through to the repository.

Jest unit tests exist under tests/unit/modules/notification/ that mock the pg pool (jest.mock of src/shared/db/connection) and cover snake_case-to-camelCase mapping, null handling, optional-client passthrough, id generation, and timestamp-at-write-time; the suite passes with no real database access.

constraints: Honor no-any: use unknown with type guards instead of any (e.g. for the status union type guard and row mapping).
Honor no-direct-db-outside-repository: all SQL lives in PgNotificationRepository; the service never touches the pool or issues queries.
No hardcoded secrets and no @gestalt/* package dependencies.

Import other modules only through their index.ts barrels; the notification module depends only on shared-types (src/shared/types/) and the pg PoolClient type — no dependency on leave, balance, audit, employee, policy, or leave-type.
Use raw parameterized pg SQL (no Knex/ORM) via pool.query, matching the audit repository pattern.
The status field is restricted to the four-value union 'PENDING'|'SENT'|'READ'|'ARCHIVED'; type is a plain string (not an enum).
outOfScope: No HTTP routes, controller, or Fastify registration for notifications — the leave module (Phase 6) is the only consumer and wires notification fanout.
No BullMQ/background job or email/push delivery — status 'SENT' is a state marker only; actual transport is out of scope.
No Knex migration or schema DDL for the notifications table — the conceptual table is defined in the reconciled architecture but migration creation is not part of this phase.
No RBAC/auth guards on notification operations — authorization is enforced at the consuming route layer, not in this module.

entityInvariants.invariant: A Notification is created with status 'PENDING' and readAt null; its status may only ever be one of PENDING, SENT, READ, ARCHIVED, and readAt is set only when the notification transitions to READ (otherwise null).
relatedEntityType and relatedEntityId are either both present (a link to a related entity such as a leave request) or both null; they are never partially set.
recipientId references an existing employee (conceptual FK recipient_id -> employees.id); createdAt is immutable once written.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Persists a notification row and returns the persisted Notification; accepts an optional PoolClient as the last argument for unit-of-work participation.
Returns the Notification or null when no row matches; accepts an optional PoolClient as the last argument.
Returns notifications for a recipient (optionally filtered by status), ordered newest-first; accepts an optional PoolClient as the last argument.
Transitions a notification's status (e.g. PENDING->SENT, SENT->READ, ->ARCHIVED) and sets readAt when transitioning to READ; accepts an optional PoolClient as the last argument.
Service operation that builds a Notification (generating id and createdAt, coercing absent optionals to null) and persists it via the repository, passing the optional client through.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Reuse the shared pg Pool exported from src/shared/db/connection.ts as the default DB executor; do not create a new Pool.

Match the audit module's model/repository/service/index layout, interface-in-model convention, optional-client-as-last-param pattern, snake_case row mapping with type-guard fallback, and service id/timestamp/null-coercion behavior.
Match the audit test conventions: jest.mock the shared connection pool, mock the repository interface, and assert mapping/null/passthrough/id/timestamp behavior with no real DB access.
Use the shared error types (e.g. NotFoundError) from src/shared/types/errors.ts for typed error semantics rather than ad-hoc errors.

The Notification entity fields and status union must match the reconciled architecture's Notification entity and the notifications conceptual table (recipient_id FK -> employees.id; indexes on recipient_id, status, and (related_entity_type, related_entity_id)).

integrationPoints.why: Shared pg Pool used as the default executor for all repository queries.
Shared typed error classes (e.g. NotFoundError) for repository/service error semantics.
Optional last-parameter client for unit-of-work participation in the leave orchestrator's transaction (Phase 6).
